svg.font-family: Hanken Grotesk, Segoe UI, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif
svg.aria-label: The seven rungs of crucible's verdict function, in the order it checks them. A claim with no falsification condition, no measurement, a measurement bound to a different claim, a deviation that is not a number, or a tolerance that was widened after the claim sealed one all return UNVERIFIABLE. A deviation within tolerance returns MATCH, and that row carries the mark because it is the only rung on which a claim stands. A deviation over tolerance returns DRIFT.

text.font-family: Conso, ui-monospace, Cascadia Mono, Consolas, monospace

g.text: Measured, compared, and broken. This is the rung that says so, with the
deviation and the tolerance in the grounds.

svg.text: verdict_for is pure and holds no model, so a verdict recomputes from the stored record and asserting one confidently changes nothing. The rungs are ordered and the
first that applies decides. Five of the seven return UNVERIFIABLE, which is fail-closed: an axis that cannot be measured is never read as holding. The
widened-tolerance rung is the one that stops a verdict being rescued after the fact.
